item.title: Former Japan PM Yasuo Fukuda, the country’s first second-generation leader, dies at 90
item.description: Yasuo Fukuda, who served as Japan's Prime Minister from 2007 to 2008, has died at the age of 90. He aimed to improve diplomatic relations with China during his short tenure in office. Fukuda hosted Chinese President Hu Jintao in a landmark visit to Japan. He faced significant domestic political challenges that led to his resignation in 2008.
item.dc:creator: Trisha Mahajan

item.title: Indian woman loses job in Ireland over visa delays, turns deportation notice into comedy
item.description: An Indian woman who moved to Ireland in 2022 to study at Trinity College Dublin is now using her real deportation notice in stand-up comedy performances. Jaishree Malik, 25, lost her job after delays in extending her immigration permission left her unable to work. Despite receiving further job offers, she could not resolve her visa status and now plans to return to India voluntarily on November 14.

item.title: Mecca country officials to hold joint meeting in Tehran; discuss regional security
item.description: Senior officials from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Turkey are set to visit Tehran for a joint meeting. This will be the first high-level contact since the renewed Houthi conflict escalated. The meeting aims to discuss regional security, drawing on Iran's experience with national security. Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure have increased, prompting military responses from the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Tharoor On Lula Victory: Congress MP hails Brazil poll result; warns on Brazil–US tensions
item.description: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor welcomed Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s re-election as Brazil’s president in a recent post. Tharoor emphasized Lula’s commitment to social inclusion, economic justice, and poverty alleviation after his closely contested victory. The election reflects Brazil’s preference for democratic resilience and cooperation amid rising right-wing movements in Latin America. Issues surrounding the voting process emerged, with disputes raised by both campaigns before result announcements.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Minnesota farmer's 300-acre farm at centre of will dispute; 2026 court ruling reverses estate reopening
item.description: In a significant Minnesota inheritance case, the state Court of Appeals has reinstated a 2017 ruling concerning the estate of farmer Clarence Vatthauer. Disputes arose from conflicting wills dated 1982 and 1989, leading to a previous court's decision being vacated. The appeals court's ruling underscored the necessity of procedural compliance and the need for finality in estate administration, reshaping the understanding of inheritance law.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Beyoncé's childhood home in Houston finds buyer as fans flock to see the property
item.description: Beyonce's childhood home in Houston, Texas, found a buyer after being listed for $1.275 million in April 2026. Her family purchased the 1935 property in 1987 and lived there until 1994. The 4,010-square-foot house has undergone extensive renovations, including upgrades to its kitchen, bedrooms and outdoor spaces. Its connection to the singer attracted multiple offers and interest from fans across the United States.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Artist bought a Giacometti chandelier for £250 in London; decades later, it sold for £2.922 million
item.description: A chandelier created by Alberto Giacometti sold for £2.922 million at a Christie's auction in February 2023. Originally purchased for £250 by British artist John Craxton in the 1960s, it remained in his family until his death. The chandelier was commissioned by art patron Peter Watson for the literary magazine Horizon, which published many famous authors. It underwent extensive authentication process before its auction, confirming its historical significance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Leafy spurge may have arrived in North America through a Massachusetts ballast dump in 1827
item.description: Leafy spurge is an invasive plant that was first recorded in Newbury, Massachusetts, in 1827. It spread rapidly across the northern United States and southern Canada during the early 1900s. By this time, it was established in several states and regions, including Ontario and Iowa. The plant has significant ecological impacts, often replacing native vegetation and causing issues for grazing animals.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Trump Claims Trade Imbalance: accuses Canada of exploiting US; says deal likely but no rush
item.description: Donald Trump has voiced concerns that Canada has been exploiting trade advantages over the United States for years. He asserts that talks between the nations are nearing a satisfactory agreement for the U.S. economy. Trump advocates for a sustainable deal rather than a temporary fix, criticizing Canadian tariffs and calling for transparency in trade practices. Despite the friction, he remains hopeful for a resolution to the ongoing trade conflict.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: ABBA’s Chiquitita raised over $5 million for UNICEF in 45 years; how the 1979 hit continues to protect children
item.description: ABBA's song Chiquitita has raised over US$5 million for UNICEF since its release in 1979. This funding supports various programs aimed at protecting vulnerable children from abuse and violence. The pledge originated during a concert at the United Nations to promote children's rights. In 2021, ABBA extended its support by pledging royalties from another song to UNICEF.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Saudi Arabia’s Singapore plan: How Riyadh aims to protect Asian oil supplies from 2027
item.description: Saudi Arabia is set to store crude oil in Singapore starting in the second half of 2027. This arrangement aims to enhance energy security in the region amid supply disruptions. Singapore's Jurong Rock Caverns will provide storage facilities for Saudi crude oil supplies. The agreement will allow Saudi Aramco to bring supplies closer to key Asian markets.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: 'Utilizing Iran for politics': IDF chief, Netanyahu clash over military action ahead of Israel elections - report
item.description: Tension brews within Israel's leadership as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and IDF chief Eyal Zamir disagree on possible military action against Iran. This clash before elections raises eyebrows about political motives behind military strategies. Netanyahu highlights the imminent threat Iran poses and urges immediate action during Trump's administration. As the election approaches, Netanyahu faces tight competition from Gadi Eisenkot, suggesting possible political deadlock with no clear majority in view.

item.title: 'Had enough': Thousands protest in Prague against Czech government's public media funding overhaul
item.description: Thousands gathered in Prague to protest government proposals affecting public television and radio funding. The planned changes would replace licence fees with state budget allocations, raising concerns about media independence. Critics argue that these measures may expose broadcasters to political pressure and reduce their financial stability. Public media employees announced plans for a strike on November 3, with a larger rally scheduled for November 15.

item.title: Riyadh airport partially reopens: Saudi intercepts Houthi ballistic missile, drones
item.description: A Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, claiming to protect the capital. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree described King Khalid International Airport as unsafe for travellers and staff. The airport administration designated terminals for domestic and international flights despite warnings. Additionally, attacks against Yemeni civilian sites by Saudi warplanes were claimed to be extensive. Claims made by both sides regarding missile interceptions and airstrikes remain unverified.
